title: Authentication vs Authorization
intro: They sound alike but answer two different questions. Mixing them up is a common source of security bugs.

slides.heading: Authentication
slides.subtitle: Who are you?
points: Passwords, one-time codes, passkeys or social login

slides.heading: Authorization
slides.subtitle: What are you allowed to do?
points: Must be enforced on the server

slides.heading: Sessions
slides.subtitle: The server remembers who you are.
points: Server stores the session, browser keeps an ID cookie
Easy to log a user out by deleting the session

slides.heading: JWT
slides.subtitle: A signed token the client carries.
points: Holds user info signed by the server
Can be verified without a database lookup
Hard to revoke, so keep expiry short

cta: Do you prefer sessions or JWTs in your projects?
